clue.text: Sweet girl in favour of breaking up legal action

blocks.note: 'Sweet Sue' is the girl of a well-known old song
to be for something is to be in favour of it
a divorce is the breaking up of a marriage

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman backs a couple splitting up and taking each other to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like padding, but 'Sweet Sue' is a song title, so the pair of words points to one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Petitioning a court to end a marriage is a formal lawsuit, one kind of proceeding taken before judges.

clue.text: Old city to boycott district in spreading town

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
to boycott something is to ban it
a district is an area

explanation.surface: Residents of an old city plan to shun one quarter of a sprawling town.
explanation.definitionFit: A built-up zone of streets and housing is what a growing town covers as it sprawls outward.

clue.text: Brother unwell, one's gathered

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Frater or Friar, a religious brother
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A sick monk is visited, and someone has collected his things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's gathered' sounds like a person collecting something; it is a description of a piece of fabric that is gathered into folds.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative strip of cloth pleated or ruched along one edge is made by gathering the material.

clue.text: About a spy with means of creating chemical effect

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a spy is an agent

explanation.surface: A tale about a secret agent equipped with some chemical weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance added to a mixture to bring about a reaction is the laboratory's tool for producing change.

clue.text: Set apart because I'm very slow?

blocks.note: read as I, with the 'm (am) understood in the phrase
so means very, as in so tired
a slow clock or train runs late

explanation.surface: Someone is kept aside from others because they are always dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'm of I'm is understood rather than written, so the answer reads as a slowcoach's apology with the verb dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone or something separate from others, as in quarantine, is to place it apart.

clue.text: Do Tom and Maud dance with the wallflower?

definitions.text: Do Tom and Maud dance with the wallflower?

blocks.clueFragment: Do Tom and Maud dance with the wallflower?
blocks.note: surface: a question about whether a couple will include a shy guest in their dance
setter's reading: when two pair off, the third person is left over and excluded

explanation.surface: At a dance, a couple wonders whether to invite the shy person by the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the role the wallflower plays: with Tom and Maud dancing together, the lone third person is excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: The one person left over or not fitting in with a group is the classic description of the leftover third.

clue.text: Altered company rig features a dog

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's modified oil rig has a dog on board.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-legged Welsh herding breed favoured by the Queen is a well-known kind of dog.

clue.text: Ronnie's strange attitude, a policy of passive obedience?

indicators.note: a strange version of the name is an odd, distorted form, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the name with its possessive s, taken letter by letter
a stance is an attitude or position on something

explanation.surface: A man called Ronnie has the odd habit of meekly doing as he is told.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to fight back against authority, even when unjust, is the doctrine of submitting without opposition.

clue.text: Keep back the flower to be embodied in a new form

definitions.text: to be embodied in a new form
definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: the answer is the act of being reborn this way

blocks.note: to rein in or rein back a horse is to keep it back
a carnation is a flower

explanation.surface: Someone holds back a bloom so it can be reborn in another shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth of a soul in a fresh body after death is the belief described by being given a new physical form.

clue.text: It's necessary to score goal, Bob:  it'll make a change!

indicators.note: to make a change is to alter the order, so the letters named before are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, from the start of it'll

explanation.surface: A football coach tells Bob that a goal is needed now and will turn the game around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like football but is a musical score. The definition borrows the clue's opening words, so 'It's' does double work.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this term marks an instrumental part that must be played and cannot be left out of the written score.

clue.text: In return rid, for example, of doleful song

indicators.note: something in return comes back the way it went, so each word is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
eg is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Someone, in exchange, gets freed of a mournful tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece turns round on its own, rather than the pair being turned as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow lament sung at a funeral is a mournful piece of music.

clue.text: Actual name adopted, or something of that kidney!

indicators.note: a child adopted is taken into a family, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: actual means real
n is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A genuine name is taken on, or something of that sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of that kidney' is an idiom for 'of that kind', but here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing anything relating to the kidneys, as in a medical ward, comes from Latin for those organs.

clue.text: Origin of oriental parent and people

blocks.note: E for east, the oriental direction
ma is mother, a parent
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A question of the roots of an Eastern mother and her race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flowing out from a source, and the act of issuing from it, is how a thing comes into being.

clue.text: Attendant monarch in the lead received by saint

indicators.note: what is received by someone is taken in and held, so these words sit inside another

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the van is the lead, the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A royal helper walking at the head of the procession is welcomed by a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN, short for vanguard, means the front position.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who waits on another, such as a household helper, is someone who attends.

clue.text: Inclined to be expansive?

blocks.note: first meaning: sloping, with a fairly sharp gradient
second meaning: overpriced, with the question mark flagging a play on expensive

explanation.surface: Someone is described as tending to be open and expansive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to' looks like 'tending to', but 'Inclined' is a slope; 'expansive' with its question mark nudges toward expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a price rather high in casual speech uses the same phrase as describing a moderately sharp gradient.

clue.text: Notes about toxic mixture make a strange collection

indicators.note: about means around, so the notes go round the outside of the other letters
a mixture is stirred up, so the word before it has its letters jumbled

blocks.note: two musical notes, E and A
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scribbled notes about a poisonous brew form an odd assortment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual objects from faraway lands gathered together form a collection of curiosities.

clue.text: Current kind? By no means!

blocks.note: what is in is current or fashionable
clement means kind or merciful

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the present weather is mild, and is told emphatically not.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'in clement', current and kind, while the whole clue, with its denial, describes the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh, stormy weather is described as not mild, and the word also means unmerciful in older use.

clue.text: Mainly ill?

blocks.note: surface: asking whether someone is for the most part unwell
setter's reading: on the main, the sea, and so unwell from the waves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly'; the main is a poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea caused by a ship's rolling motion is the illness suffered by passengers at sea.

clue.text: Air hack, possibly, in Pakistan

definitions.note: a place in Pakistan: the answer is a city there

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several possible arrangements of the letters given

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A travel writer, perhaps a hack for an airline, is reporting from Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city and chief port of the country lies on the Arabian Sea coast.

clue.text: Vessel I'm able to see in Rome

blocks.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids
I'm able means I can

explanation.surface: A tourist has a large tub and is able to go sightseeing in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not the verb but a noun: a bishop's see, here the Holy See.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal seat and its city-state inside Rome is the bishopric of the Pope, the Holy See.

clue.text: Chatty book on blue letters

indicators.note: the letters of a word may be set out in any order, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: vol is the abbreviation for volume, a book
taken as written

explanation.surface: A talkative book about risque correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks fluently and at length is described as talkative and garrulous.

clue.text: Lancaster's corruption of forebears

indicators.note: a corruption is a debased, altered form, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: The decline of a noble house traced back through its line.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster is an English city and a royal house, which suits a clue about lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything inherited from or relating to one's grandparents and earlier family is described as coming from ancestors.

clue.text: A hundred and four organised the island

indicators.note: something organised has been arranged, so the letters of the number are put in a new order

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tour party of one hundred and four people arranged a trip to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek holiday spot in the Ionian Sea is an island off the north-west coast of Greece.

clue.text: Sheepish sound when the French go in to bat

indicators.note: to go in to something is to enter it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An awkward noise from a team when the French come in to take their innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' means embarrassed in the surface, but here it means made by a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a sheep or goat is its characteristic call.

clue.text: Wood found in herbal salts

indicators.note: found in says the answer is lying inside the words that come next

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Splinters of timber turn up in a pot of bath salts.
explanation.definitionFit: A very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for model aircraft, is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Five in mixed race group are cut up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
something mixed has been jumbled, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people within a mixed-race group are deeply upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' looks like the British idiom for upset, but it is meant literally: to slice, as with a joint of meat. 'group' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice cooked meat into portions at the table is to divide it with a knife.

clue.text: Gentleman caller holds a degree, love!

indicators.note: what holds something has it inside, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
love is nil in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A visiting gentleman has a university qualification and greets his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a gentleman or horseman is used in English for a courteous man.

clue.text: Amaze individual in spontaneous event

blocks.note: to amaze is to surprise
in legal language a party is an individual, as in the guilty party

explanation.surface: Someone astonishes a lone person at an unplanned celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration kept secret from its guest of honour seems to that person to burst out unplanned.
